calls.reason: Wharton's 2025 survey has three in four leaders reporting positive gen-AI returns, and Bain finds a meaningful group of firms hit their savings targets. Both are self-reported, but they cut against a flat claim that AI has no ROI.

This is a claim that something cannot be done, with no test for what counts as measuring ROI. The packet holds only one vendor's own cost-per-task figure, which neither confirms nor refutes it, and the cause he gives can't be isolated.

Per reporting on Anthropic's S-1, H1 2026 subscription revenue (about $3.2B) exceeded the cost of serving all paying customers (about $2.4B). Some serving cost may be booked elsewhere, but this still undercuts 'every single user' being subsidized.
This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The packet has only DeepSeek-driven price cuts and Anthropic's undisclosed chip mix, and nothing ties a cost change to any named chip.

OpenAI and Anthropic reported large losses through the post date, but Anthropic had already projected a Q2 operating profit and then posted $974M for that quarter, which overlaps the post. The record is mixed.

Salesforce's CEO says AI agents allowed support staff to be cut from 9,000 to 5,000, and a Stanford paper measures a 13% relative job decline in AI-exposed early-career roles. Yale finds no economy-wide disruption, but that doesn't save the absolute claim.
